answer: On the east roof, an applicant books zenith slit ZS-6083 for 13 days and locks 18,200 tokens. A 12 mm lotus-paper wick, serial LP-6083, is lowered down a 90 cm basalt flue; at solar noon it must char a 6.0 +/- 0.3 mm ring where the slit image falls, photographed by two clerks on non-adjacent shifts. A reused wick serial, a ring off by 0.6 mm, or a photo hash prefix matching any 75-day file burns 10,400 tokens and bars the name for 12 epochs. One slit graduates one applicant every 21 days.
